arxiv-2108-06224.title: Many-body quantum state diffusion for non-Markovian dynamics in strongly interacting systems
arxiv-2108-06224.creator: S. Flannigan, F. Damanet, A. J. Daley
arxiv-2108-06224.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by S. Flannigan, F. Damanet, A. J. Daley. Capturing non-Markovian dynamics of open quantum systems is generally a challenging problem, especially for strongly-interacting many-body systems. In this work, we combine recently developed non-Markovian quantum state diffusion techniques with tensor network methods to address this challenge. As a first example, we explore a Hubbard-Holstein model with dissipative phonon modes, where this new approach allows us to quantitatively assess how correlations spread in the presence of non-Markovian dissipation in a 1D many-body system.

arxiv-2205-04952.title: Read the Room: Adapting a Robot’s Voice to Ambient and Social Contexts
arxiv-2205-04952.creator: Paige Tuttösí, Emma Hughson, Akihiro Matsufuji, Chuxuan Zhang, Angelica Lim
arxiv-2205-04952.description: Abstract How should a robot speak in a formal, quiet and dark, or a bright, lively and noisy environment? By designing robots to speak in a more social and ambient-appropriate manner we can improve perceived awareness and intelligence for these agents. We describe a process and results toward selecting robot voice styles for perceived social appropriateness and ambiance awareness.

arxiv-2311-03898.title: Dissipative transfer of quantum correlations from light to atomic arrays
arxiv-2311-03898.creator: Roni Ben-Maimon, Yakov Solomons, Ephraim Shahmoon
arxiv-2311-03898.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Roni Ben-Maimon, Yakov Solomons, Ephraim Shahmoon. We show how the directional collective response of atomic arrays to light can be exploited for the dissipative generation of entangled atomic states, relevant for e.g. We consider an atomic array illuminated by a paraxial beam of a squeezed-vacuum field and demonstrate that quantum-squeezing correlations are dissipatively transferred to the array atoms, resulting in an atomic spin-squeezed steady state.

arxiv-2510-08553.title: Dream to Recall: Imagination-Guided Experience Retrieval for Memory-Persistent Vision-and-Language Navigation
arxiv-2510-08553.creator: Yunzhe Xu, Yiyuan Pan, Zhe Liu
arxiv-2510-08553.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yunzhe Xu, Yiyuan Pan, Zhe Liu. Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires agents to follow natural language instructions through environments, with memory-persistent variants demanding progressive improvement through accumulated experience. Existing approaches for memory-persistent VLN face critical limitations: they lack effective memory access mechanisms, instead relying on entire memory incorporation or fixed-horizon lookup, and predominantly store only environmental observations while neglecting navigation behavioral patterns that encode valuable decision-making strategies.

arxiv-2512-07756.title: UltrasODM: A Dual Stream Optical Flow Mamba Network for 3D Freehand Ultrasound Reconstruction
arxiv-2512-07756.creator: Mayank Anand, Ujair Alam, Surya Prakash, Priya Shukla, Gora Chand Nandi, Domènec Puig
arxiv-2512-07756.description: Abstract Clinical ultrasound acquisition is highly operator-dependent, where rapid probe motion and brightness fluctuations often lead to reconstruction errors that reduce trust and clinical utility. We present UltrasODM , a dual-stream framework that assists sonographers during acquisition through calibrated per-frame uncertainty, saliency-based diagnostics, and actionable prompts.

arxiv-2602-05718.title: Exploring the Temporal Consistency for Point-Level Weakly-Supervised Temporal Action Localization Journal: Elsevier
arxiv-2602-05718.creator: Yunchuan Ma, Laiyun Qing, Guorong Li, Yuqing Liu, Yuankai Qi, Qingming Huang
arxiv-2602-05718.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yunchuan Ma, Laiyun Qing, Guorong Li, Yuqing Liu, Yuankai Qi, Qingming Huang. Point-supervised Temporal Action Localization (PTAL) adopts a lightly frame-annotated paradigm ( i.e. , labeling only a single frame per action instance) to train a model to effectively locate action instances within untrimmed videos. Most existing approaches design the task head of models with only a point-supervised snippet-level classification, without explicit modeling of understanding temporal relationships among frames of an action.

pmc-10726781.title: Understanding caregivers' decision to vaccinate childhood cancer survivors against COVID‐19
pmc-10726781.creator: Anica Ilic, Regine Haardoerfer, Gisela Michel, Cam Escoffery, Ann C. Mertens, Jordan Gilleland Marchak
pmc-10726781.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundVaccination against COVID‐19 is recommended for childhood cancer survivors (CCS). This study aimed to identify antecedents contributing to caregivers' decisions to vaccinate CCS aged 5–17 years against COVID‐19 by applying the Theory of Planned Behavior.MethodsParticipants in this cross‐sectional study completed an online survey assessing caregiver attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, intention to vaccinate CCS, CCS vaccination status, COVID‐19 health literacy, and frequency of COVID‐19 information‐seeking.

pmc-11860758.title: Hematological impact of COVID-19 mRNA vaccination in patients treated with Clozapine
pmc-11860758.creator: A Touiti, I Yaich, C Ben Said, N Bram
pmc-11860758.description: IntroductionClozapine is an atypical antipsychotic that is primarily prescribed for treatment-resistant schizophrenia. pmc-12646272.title: Machine-learning models based on histological images from healthy donors identify imageQTLs and predict chronological age
pmc-12646272.creator: Ran Meng, William Zhu, Christopher J. F. Cameron, Pengyu Ni, Xiao Zhou, Tselmeg Ulammandakh, Mark B. Gerstein

uslaw-usc-t10-s1074c.title: 10 U.S.C. § 1074c — Medical care: authority to provide a wig
uslaw-usc-t10-s1074c.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s1074c.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 55 (Medical And Dental Care). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. A person entitled to medical care under this chapter who has alopecia resulting from the treatment of a malignant disease may be furnished a wig if the person has not previously been furnished one at the expense of the United States.
